en: A sack full of flour on which chickens sat and it became moist from their droppings—one should sift the dough outward and the rest is permitted. (Beit Yosef in name of R' Eliezer of Garmiza)

He should take in his hand and afterward must sift all the remaining flour (Maharshal); and so is the custom. Flour in a sack that mice bit—its law is likewise: if before Passover one must sift the flour; if crumbs like dry dough crumbs remain on the sieve they are discarded and the flour may be retained until after Passover. If found thus on Passover it is forbidden for benefit and sifting does not help. If the sack rests in its place without shaking and the flour did not mix, he takes in his hand the bitten place and ties the sack there under the bite with some flour; the remainder may be retained by sifting; nevertheless it is forbidden to eat on Passover. All this only when it appears the mice ate some of the flour; but if they bit only the sack and there is doubt perhaps they ate nothing—even if found on Passover it may be retained and is forbidden to eat; even if found thus before Passover, lest there is chametz that dried and crumbles. (My teacher in Bach siman 453) But the Gaon Maharam of Lublin wrote in responsum siman 119 that they should take other guarded flour to make matzot for the first two nights, and flour from mouse bites they should make matzot and bake all those matzot before Passover by sifting the flour; and that sieve through which they sifted the flour—one need not be stringent and it is permitted for everything:

He chews. This is the meaning of melogma as written siman 442; and Rokeach wrote that even if he already chewed and placed on his wound before Passover he must destroy and remove them—end. And so explained above siman 442 that any melogma not spoiled before Passover requires destruction—not like Beit Hillel YD siman 255 who wrote that not chewing is only during Passover; but if it was already chametz it is permitted to leave on Passover on any remedy—end. In truth this is not so; and the main difficulty that forced this distinction is from what Rambam wrote that when not in the manner of enjoyment, such as melogma for a wound, one may heal from chametz on Passover—initially there is none, for there it is gentile chametz (and no Jewish responsibility on it; Magen Avraham wrote further a remedy that the Jew buy the flour for the gentile and make melogma on eve of holiday, and Pri Chadash doubts much, for it should only be like a gift where we require recognizable action that he does not wish to accept—and here the opposite). It discusses unlike Jewish chametz as Kesef Mishneh wrote and so Magen Avraham and in responsum Emunat Shmuel siman 27. All this for illness without danger; but with danger even through the Jew himself from his chametz it is also permitted, so Magen Avraham and responsum Emunat Shmuel there and above siman 465 seif 2. Chametz that passed Passover is permitted—Chafetz Chayim see there. (Melogma path even without danger; eating only where danger—Rashba) Pri Chadash wrote: I was asked about one with frequent headache who places a poultice of flour and water and other drugs on his temples to ease pain—whether permitted on Passover; he answered forbidden; and concludes there indeed with fruit juice it is fine—see there:
His wound. But to chew and swallow immediately is permitted for it does not leaven immediately. Magen Avraham:

For saliva. Even if she expectorated blood—and it is explained in seif (4) [5] that blood does not leaven—nevertheless it is impossible without saliva flecks; and this is specifically when sucking. Chafetz Chayim:

Nullified. This does not refer to nullification before Passover, for this was not in the category of nullification once it leavened afterward as siman 446; rather since he gave before his animal it was nullified and he renounced it from his mind; nevertheless it is good to give them little by little so they leave none. Chafetz Chayim see there:

Saliva. Bach wrote that Mordechai also forbids only when saliva is found; so in Shach; and he challenged the Rav here since Rokeach explained explicitly only when saliva is found (and Mahari Weil) that in unspecified one must burn all remainder—this is certainly extra stringency—end. Nevertheless it appears to me specifically in a horse and the like; but in a cow that has saliva from unspecified, certainly one must destroy from unspecified; therefore give before it little by little as written:

The wall. And likewise a wooden wall—Magen Avraham see there. Chafetz Chayim wrote: it appears specifically when sweating from itself or from fire heat; but if sweating from heat and steam of hot blood it is like water that makes fit for all—see there:

They forbid. Or Zarua wrote that the permitters' view is primary and Magen Avraham wrote the forbidders' view is primary; good to retain until after Passover—Chafetz Chayim. See Tur that wrote regarding dry meat sweating from water it was rinsed in—its sweat leavens; and above siman 453 s.k. 15 from law of animal sweat:
The moistened. And it implies the rest of the flour is permitted even on Passover; nevertheless afterward sift—Bach and Maharshal and Taz wrote this is mere stringency—see there:
Impossible. Such as when moistened in many places:

He should sift. The moistened place will be like dough and remain above. It appears if he need not eat from the flour on yom tov it is forbidden to sift on yom tov—see siman 507—rather sift through a gentile to destroy chametz; or give to gentile as gift before it stood mil measure—Magen Avraham. (See siman 446 and 459):

Sifting. But if he takes in hand all the moistened place it helps even if dried—Chafetz Chayim and so Taz; even during Passover he permits in such case—for only where entire sack or large part moistened then impossible to take moist place; but if possible to take moist place—it is permitted. Chafetz Chayim:

And mixes. Although flour in flour is called wet in wet and we do not say it reawakens—nevertheless crumbs are different for they do not mix well and reawaken as siman 467 seif 4; therefore forbidden to eat and permitted to retain. But if dried on Passover it is like chametz mixed on Passover—for while moist it did not mix, therefore mixed on Passover and forbidden to retain—Magen Avraham. Or Zarua wrote: where doubt whether moistened from fruit juice etc. or leavening things—lenient to eat on Passover even if dried from double doubt perhaps fruit juice, and if you say other things perhaps nothing mixed—see there. Bach wrote: mice bit sack and ate flour and dried—before Passover sift flour, discard crumbs on sieve, flour may be retained; if found thus on Passover all forbidden for benefit. If sack unmoved without shaking, take bitten place (with some flour), tie sack there, sift, may retain, nevertheless forbidden to eat on Passover—all when visible mouse ate flour; if bit only sack and doubt perhaps ate nothing—even found on Passover may retain, forbidden to eat, even before Passover lest chametz dried and crumbles—end. Maharam of Lublin siman 119 ruled on sack bitten by mice: if baked matzot before Passover from that flour—not forbidden to eat on Passover except first two nights take other guarded flour; flour sifted from that sieve—no stringency, permitted for all—end. Taz wrote even if water fell and dried, if he recognizes moist place take it and sift rest; certainly for mouse bites take around bitten place, sift rest and eat on Passover—end. Magen Avraham wrote: in mice be more stringent, these mice are wicked and go through whole sack and eat, especially in barrel—therefore Geonim were stringent—end. So Mabit for this reason. Chafetz Chayim agreed like Taz to tie bitten place and permit rest by sifting in every case—end. Only when no moisture visible at bite; but if any moisture at bite, attribute to common thing perhaps mice urinated on flour—etc.:

And milk. Likewise milk in brine even boiling and clear, and certainly congealed—Shach. And above siman 462 from law of fat; Magen Avraham wrote likewise bile does not leaven (it is only moisture and blood) and therefore permitted to make dough for healing; Pri Chadash wrote likewise milk water does not leaven. In Halakhot Ketanot part 2 siman 211 wrote sweat leavens—see there. See Shach. Chicken droppings do not leaven—Tur. Likewise wheat in animal dung—Rokeach. In human excrement Chafetz Chayim is stringent—see there. Plain that all Tur and Mechaber wrote here that leaven—if stood without occupation for leavening time, for through occupation it does not come to leaven:
Mishnah Pesachim 35
Tur; and Mordechai wrote so in name of Rokeach chapter 3 of Pesachim
Tur in name of his father Rosh chapter 2 of Pesachim
Tur in name of R' Eliezer of Garmiza
There (in that source)
Darkei Moshe in name of R' Yitzchak of Vienna chapter 2 of Pesachim
Yerushalmi
R' Yerucham and Orchot Chayim
There in Orach Chayim
Braita there 39
There in Gemara
Rosh there
462—one who gives—learn from 461:
But in it and already nullified—meaning if nullified before coming to prohibition; and since rabbinic matter we do not establish prohibition in such case:
And some are stringent. For unspecified they have saliva as chapter 20 of Shabbos 102b and above end of siman 324:
463—sack, etc.

And some forbid. He holds it comes from moisture in it and compares to saliva which is offspring of water and makes fit as above. Book Rashogah compares to human sweat that does not leaven as seif 5 and also does not make fit like sweat—thus not offspring of water unlike saliva and armpit sweat that make fit—there chapter 6 mishnah 5 and mishnah 7:
464—he should take in hand. As Yerushalmi brings Rosh chapter 21 seif 13: one of R' Pedai's cases—a sack of oil in wheat storehouse—asked R' Bun: go scrape beneath you:
And if impossible, etc. As chapter 21: remove its place:
And specifically, etc. Magen Avraham s.k. 8:

465—dew leavens. Yerushalmi chapter 3 end halacha 1: one said on herbs permitted, on gleanings forbidden; another switches—R' Chanania son of R' Hillel: even per one who permits on herbs, on gleanings from six hours onward dew damages them; although at four hours dew melts, moisture does not pass until heat of day. They also said Yerushalmi end Terumot halacha 2: R' Yochanan in name of Rashbi—if one says seven liquids, tell him dew and water are one kind and they counted two—see there and in verse 'and he wrung full bowl of water':
And likewise urine, etc. As chapter 6 of Machshirin mishnah 5—they are offspring of water:
But blood and milk. They are seven liquids not included in water like urine and the rest; Yerushalmi spoke only of dew as above; in milk they said chapter 21 Yoma 1, etc.:
And human sweat. Pesachim 39b: she spat on her dry meat—even sweat on her meat; Rashash there:
466—and bake immediately. For l'chatchila forbidden even moment as siman 459 seif 2:
And if doubtful. For it is d'oraisa doubt:

Sack full of flour that became moist—Pri Chadash wrote: sack full of flour buried in sand and flour found moist is chametz, for we learned chapter 3 Machshirin: burying in sand is in ki yutan; Raavad wrote there is no sand without water:

And if impossible, etc., sift flour, etc.—this is Rokeach's view; although Rosh wrote on this view it is great leniency, Mechaber relied since Mordechai agrees—only when dried Mordechai also stringent like Rosh; Mechaber ruled stringently not like Rokeach. See Netziv and Magen Alef who appear not to have decided this:

And if dried on Passover, etc.—see Mishna Berurah. Shulchan Aruch implies even if sifting was on Passover may retain; Magen Alef doubts since mixing occurs through sieve holes—why permit retain? Source in Beit Yosef also requires sifting before Passover [if not sifted before Passover throw all—but no difference dried before or on Passover, only before Passover advice to sift]; Pri Megadim also strained; Magen Alef agreed Mechaber means dried before Passover has remedy by sifting, on Passover no remedy, forbidden to retain; only manner of speech that before Passover they are careful to sift—end:

And likewise urine—see Mishna Berurah. Mishnah Machshirin chapter 6: urine of adults and minors; Rosh and Raavad: adults—from urethra opening. Apparent contradiction: chicken droppings and animal dung do not leaven—Tur rules sack chickens sat on, moist from droppings, flour there not chametz [see Bach and Taz]. I found in Acharonim: thick excrement—not that truly thick how flour in sack became dough from droppings above; rather not fully soft—for if fully soft counted as urethra discharge [see Pri Megadim; it appears to me also his intent when much moisture]. In Chayei Adam two views on soft excrement: some like fruit juice, some never leavens—second is poskim who did not distinguish thick and soft; first author unknown who distinguishes—only Acharonim, leaning like urine that leavens]. Nevertheless even fully soft like water I greatly doubt: Tosefta challenged Rosh on Tiberias water—see there; without Rosh/Raavad I would say intent adult or minor urine, unlike eight-month infant in next mishnah—end. Later Rambam chapter 10 Laws Food Impurity copies mishnah—appears plain like our words [see Chut HaShani siman 30 on Rambam; Acharonim on Seder Taharot attribute to Gra explain plainly]. Many lean from Rosh due to Tosefta; therefore even soft like water same as excrement here. Chut HaShani sides even per Rosh mishnah not on soft excrement as urine for making fit—Tiberias proves—but his words leave no view on soft urine for fit and leavening. However all written per poskim who equate leavening and making fit—what counts as water offspring for fit also leavens; what not counted there not water for leavening. Some Acharonim hold not necessary—therefore urine of animal, dog, mouse leavens though Tosafeta says animal urine does not make fit [see Acharonim]; with another doubt certainly lenient as I wrote—end:

And human sweat—see Mishna Berurah. On chicken droppings, Maamar Mordechai 104 ruled one who bought wheat sack found dry cat droppings—permitted for Passover; though one should not learn from chicken droppings in Rokeach—birds differ for no urine concern as non-nurslings lack urine place (Shaarei Shamayim maamar 4); cats one may fear urination like dung placed there and leavened—nevertheless do not establish prohibition; perhaps no urine or far from wheat or perhaps not leavened; even if slightly leavened only minority of minority; urine law disputed in Beit Yosef; Pri Chadash and Chafetz Chayim: only human urine leavens—without visible spoilage in wheat do not be stringent else no grain without this doubt—primary—end:

A man shall not chew. This is melogma as above siman 442 s.k. 7; Rokeach siman 291 wrote even if chewed and placed on wound before Passover requires destruction—end; explained above siman 442 all melogma not spoiled before Passover requires destruction—plain from Talmud and poskim above siman 442—not like Beit Hillel YD 255 s.k. 3 who wrote not chewing only during Passover; if already chametz permitted on Passover for remedy—so Kesef Mishneh in name of Rashba Pesach laws—end. In truth all this is not so; what Kesef Mishneh wrote I toiled and did not find this distinction. Main difficulty forcing distinction: Rambam chapter 5 Foundations of Torah permits healing not in manner of enjoyment like melogma for wound from chametz on Passover—initially none, there gentile chametz (unlike Jewish as Kesef Mishneh and Magen Avraham and Maharash Kaidenburg responsum 27). All for illness without danger; with danger even Jew from his chametz permitted—Magen Avraham, Yerushalmi, Maharshak there, above siman 465 s.k. 2. Chametz after Passover permitted; Torat Adam to Rashba 11b: for eating perhaps Torah-level prohibition, healing only with danger—end; so Ran chapter Kol Sha'ah and Rivash 255; explained YD 255 unlike some Yerushalmi Kol Sha'ah halacha 1—even not in manner of enjoyment forbidden—see there. Pri Chadash: asked one with frequent headache placing flour-water poultice on temples—answered forbidden; concludes with fruit juice fine—end:
And place on his wound. But chew and swallow immediately permitted for does not leaven immediately—so Magen Avraham:
For saliva leavens. It appears even blood flecks—for impossible without saliva flecks as Yevamot 105: yevamah expectorated blood—chalitzah impossible without saliva flecks—specifically when sucking:

Since already nullified. Not nullification before Passover—for not in nullification category once leavened after as siman 446; rather since gave before animal nullified and renounced; though certainly chametz must burn as explained above siman 453; so animal not eat chametz as siman 448—nevertheless from unspecified we do not know leavened—no concern—plain Rav's view, unlike Magen Avraham who left requires study; nevertheless good give little by little as Mahari Weil and Maharil above siman 465 s.k. 3:

Even without visible saliva. Bach wrote Mordechai forbids only found saliva—so Shach; challenged Rav since Rokeach explained explicitly only found saliva (Mahari Weil) that burn all remainder is extra zeal—end. Nevertheless appears specifically horse etc. Rokeach siman 285; but cow has saliva from unspecified as Shabbos 141a bad-mouthed cow—above siman 324—certainly destroy from unspecified; give little by little as s.k. 4:

Wall sweat permitted. Rosh view here—like human sweat not making fit not leavening; therefore specifically sweating from itself or fire heat; if from heat and steam of hot blood—like water making fit chapter 2 Machshirin and leavens; Rivash responsum 255: sweat from liquids is like those liquids; though Rosh chapter 21 woman expectorated—appears sweat in bathhouse also does not leaven—must be from fire heat not water:

Permitted. Apparently permitted entirely—even knead with water need not bake immediately like fruit juice with water above siman 462; not true fruit juice but own derivative; Bach on chicken droppings; Hagahot Semak on mouse eating in Beit Yosef 453 and Netziv: all though not fruit juice hasten to leaven with water like fruit juice; if still moist sift and retain moist until after Passover; if dried and mixed do not knead, keep after Passover; if kneaded bake immediately as 462:

And some forbid. Maharam Mintz: wall sweats from moisture within; wooden wall may absorb water while attached—end. See Rosh chapter 4 Machshirin such is fruit juice for making fit—end. For law, Rav's son-in-law in Eshel Avraham: permitters primary; Magen Avraham forbidders primary; good retain until after Passover. Tur ruled dry meat sweating from rinse water leavens—above 453 s.k. 22 animal sweat—see there:

Water fell on flour. Bach stringent 453 on mouse-eaten flour; if bit only sack and doubt perhaps ate nothing—even found on Passover may retain. Maharam Lublin responsum 119 lenient in pressure on mouse-bitten sacks—end; Taz permits take around bite, sift rest, eat on Passover even if dried—end. Magen Avraham: mice be more stringent, wicked mice go through sack, especially barrel—Geonim stringent—end; Mabit same. It appears not stringent on mice-eaten flour—permit by sifting always—for primary law mouse-eaten flour not in early poskim—Acharonim learned from bitten wheat mouse saliva leavens as 453; even mouse saliva leavens, eating flour no leaven concern—clear proof chapter 9 Parah mishnah 3: all vermin drinking mei chatat not invalid for no saliva except weasel—R' Eliezer adds mouse—halakha not like him as Rambam chapter 9 Parah 12 no moisture from mouth; Tosafot Chullin chapter 1. Thus even liquids that absorb moisture not invalid—certainly flour each crumb separate—no concern from not eating; unlike wheat lump perhaps moisture remains from bite strength—unlike flour lenient always—clear; my mind not decisive against great Acharonim especially stringent; at least tie bite place, permit rest by sifting as Taz; stringency did not consider flour. All when no moisture at bite; if moisture visible, attribute perhaps mice urinated—see nearby s.k. 14 urine leaven concern like water moistening:
Take in hand all moist place—nevertheless afterward sift—Bach, Maharshal; Taz: mere stringency:
Sift flour. Magen Avraham: if not eating flour on yom tov forbidden sift on yom tov—sift through gentile or gift to gentile before mil measure—end:
Sifting does not help—implies; but if takes all moist place helps even dried—Taz permits even on Passover—only entire sack or large part moistened impossible take place; if possible—permitted:

And mixes with rest. Although flour in flour wet in wet, we do not say reawakens—crumbs differ, do not mix well—Acharonim agree unlike Levush requiring sixty—above 453. Rav's son-in-law Eshel Avraham in name of Derishah: doubt moist from fruit juice or leavening—lenient eat on Passover even if dried from double doubt—end; above 465 from siman end:

And likewise urine. Bach in name of Orchot Chayim: all water offspring—mouth, nose, eye, ear, urine—leaven—end. Since tied to offspring, no difference minor/adult urethra discharge as Machshirin chapter 6 mishnah 5: what is offspring of water. Though chicken dung and animal dung do not leaven (sift excrement outward per Bach bal teshaktzu) — urine of animal not called water offspring as Rambam chapter 10 Food Impurity—for making fit; Mordechai on mice urinated on wheat: do not presume chametz until visible leavening—thus Rivash and Orchot Chayim do not argue with Mordechai unlike Beit Yosef implication. Animal mouth leavens like human as above seif 2. Blood though forbidden, nullified in sixty unlike chametz in smallest amount:

And milk. Likewise milk in brine boiling clear or congealed—Shach; above 462 fat law; Magen Avraham bile does not leaven; plain all Tur/Mechaber here leaven if stood without occupation for leavening time—not worse than water—for through occupation no leaven—requires study:
And human sweat. Above s.k. 6:
Without interruption—even less than mil measure; and bake immediately implies no measure—for dripping itself not full occupation, little leavens unlike Netziv:

Seif 3: sack full of flour moist from wall sweat permitted, etc.—note see Tur on dry meat sweating leavens; Magen Avraham above 462: reason when sweating expels absorbed water—intent: rinsed with water, absorbed, though dried when sweats expels. I wondered: first rinse water, second fruit juice as YD 69—last rinse fruit juice helps—meat dried sweats—leavens or only from last fruit juice not leavening, or first water only, or both fruit juice with water stiff chametz question. This is explicit mishnah chapter 2 Orlah 13: vessels anointed impure oil then pure, or reverse—R' Eliezer: follow first; Sages: follow last—Rambam, Rosh, Raavad: when dried, sweating expels—R' Eliezer expels first, Sages last—we hold Sages—if absorbs sequentially only last expels—therefore only fruit juice water not first rinse—does not leaven—clear. Tur inserted R' Eliezer Garmiza amid Rosh words Rosh brought without dry meat—why Tur inserted, if in Rokeach why Rosh omitted, if not Rosh view why Tur ruled—requires study:

(There seif 4) water on flour or sack moistened, etc.—see Chok Yaakov lenient, proof from chapter 9 Parah. Rav Nachum Ginzburg Kraske wrote: reject proof—distinguish drinking vs eating—drinking swallows without chewing saliva; eating different—brief. I answered Chafetz Chayim proof correct: if mouse expels saliva from mouth, at least doubt expelled before/after drinking; known vermin have no saliva—if rely on this estimate even with impurity presumption, more so here no prohibition presumption but permission presumption—Chafetz Chayim correct for law—end:

[1] Shall not chew, etc.—implies permitted to chew and swallow for do not leaven immediately (Magen Avraham); Lechem Mishnah chapter Kol Sha'ah: while chewing and occupied in chewing does not leaven—end. Responsa Ramban 103 and Rashba 488: biting grain in teeth never leavens—only chewing leavens after, not mere bite—see 453 seif 3:
[2] On his wound, etc.—Jewish chametz as 453 s.k. 5 general healing laws; Rokeach: even if chewed and placed before Passover requires destruction:

[3] For saliva, etc.—Rav's son-in-law Chok Yaakov: even blood flecks impossible without saliva as Yevamot 105—when sucking—end. Requires study Levush EH 169:40 first view even without sucking impossible without saliva; actually reason perhaps all blood valid for chalitzah; study: putrid moisture does not make fit per Machshirin poskim:
[4] And some stringent, etc.—extra zeal (Bach); Acharonim more stringent—give little by little so none remains:

[5] [Levush] some permit, etc.—from Shulchan Aruch wording 'permit' in unspecified implies Mechaber tends forbid; Shulchan Aruch tends lenient as Derishah: if unknown what moistened sack—lenient even eat on Passover if dried from double doubt fruit juice or wall sweat; if water perhaps nothing fell; Rama 467 does not permit eat from double doubt—compare 467:12; end Derishah permits wall sweat entirely; Magen Avraham: most forbid—not compelled for examiner. Also what wrote Ramaz forbids—checked Ramaz on parchment, omitted; also no source for Rosh challenge to Rokeach as Imrei Kohen. Book on parchment: sack in cellar moist from humidity—wet drops—made fit from Machshirin chapter 2: house sweat, pits, caves, caves, human sweat pure; drank pure water, sweat pure; came from drawn water, sweat impure; bathed and sweat pure. Chapter 6: all fish brine presumed impure from water added; there: mouth, eye, urine major/minor make fit and impure zov, saliva, urine not impure not make fit—sweat, putrid moisture, excrement, blood, eight-month nursing. For making fit only called liquid—end much law from parchment. Chok Yaakov: if sweat from heat and steam of hot blood—all leaven:
[6] [Levush] chicken droppings, etc.—likewise wheat in animal dung (Rokeach); mei kazah does not leaven like blood and moisture (Magen Avraham):
Wheat. Even less than kezayit—Pri Chadash see 287:1:
Sift. Although sifting is father of melacha—here no waste:
Does not leaven. General rule depends what is called offspring of water—see chapter 6 Machshirin mishnah 5, Beit Yosef:
When it stops. It leavens even less than mil measure. Taz raised Rosh/Ran chapter 30—see there:

(1) [Seif 1] Shall not chew wheat, etc.—implies permitted chew and swallow for do not leaven immediately. Magen Avraham s.k. 1; Chafetz Chayim 2; Rabbi Akiva Eiger 2; Chafetz Chayim 1; Chafetz Chayim 2; Magen Avraham 1; while chewing and occupied in chewing does not leaven—Rabbi Akiva Eiger there in name of Lechem Mishnah chapter Kol Sha'ah. Rabbi Akiva Eiger 1; nevertheless clean teeth afterward lest something remain and leaven:

(2) There. Shall not chew, etc.—even less than kezayit—for though no lav by eating less than kezayit, perhaps Torah obligation destroy half-measure forbidden by Torah eating and retaining. Pri Chadash; however see Aruch HaShulchan 1 who lengthy wrote half-measure here only rabbinic; wrote permitted leave this melogma from nullified chametz if no kezayit—use on eve of holiday—end; see above 442 note 27:
(3) There. Shall not chew wheat, etc.—meaning of melogma. Chafetz Chayim 1; see above 442 seif 2 and our words there:

(4) There. Shall not chew—specifically chewing does not leaven, not mere bite; likewise mouse bite no leaven concern. Rashba responsum 488; Rabbi Akiva Eiger 1; Rabbi Akiva Eiger 1; see above 453 seif 3 and our words there:

(5) There. Place on wound, etc.—for they leaven through saliva in mouth while on wound mil measure—transgress bal yera'eh and bal yimatzei. Rabbi Zalman 3; even if chewed and placed before Passover requires destruction—Rokeach 291; Chafetz Chayim 1; Rabbi Akiva Eiger 2; Magen Avraham 2; Rabbi Zalman there. Remove when sixth hour arrives on eve unless spoiled unusable for dog as 442. Rabbi Zalman there; see seif 2 and our words there:

(6) There. Place on wound—specifically Jewish chametz—bal yera'eh; but gentile chametz loaned to Jew or placed on wound without Jewish responsibility—permitted. If no melogma for gentile, Jew buys flour, gentile makes melogma for Jew's wound. Magen Avraham s.k. 2 in name of Kesef Mishneh chapter 5 Foundations Torah 8 in name of Orchot Chayim—see there; Matitei Yehuda 448:5 agrees; Rabbi Akiva Eiger 2; Rabbi Zalman 4; likewise above 465 note 6 in name of Acharonim—see there. However Makor Chayim 1 wondered on this permission—for when places on wound totally lost, not true loan returning—no greater gift—and therefore forbids unless spoilage in gentile hands before placing as 442 before placing—see there. Pri Chadash would not permit this case—see there; though Matitei Yehuda reconciled and agreed permit—nevertheless l'chatchila stringent if possible make so spoils in gentile hands before placing or knead fruit juice or other dressing; if impossible and great pain, rely on permitters; Jew intend not acquire at all, remains gentile property while on wound until thrown to trash:
(s.k. 1) Not so, etc.—implies permitted, etc.—for otherwise since only teaching saliva leavens:
(And in s.k. following) If so should teach briefly forbidden chew and swallow and we know human saliva leavens; nevertheless such is permitted:

(s.k. 2) And place, etc.—and see YD end 255 we hold like Rambam: not in manner of enjoyment permitted for illness without danger; therefore Rambam challenged mishnah shall not chew and place on wound—therefore brought Kesef Mishneh:

Therefore must be, etc.—transgresses bal yera'eh—not benefit prohibition for not in manner of enjoyment. See Tosafot beginning 29: if Jew chews even gentile chametz—liable for responsibility even intending rob via chewing. Even intending steal via chewing liable:
They said 83 Ketubot 103:

Because difficulty, etc.—from where Talmud intended mishnah teach incidentally healing virtues of wheat for wound; perhaps law itself forbids placing on wound for benefit—but per Magen Avraham no benefit prohibition here not in manner of enjoyment. See 453:6 law wants existence. Why Pri Chadash forbids even gentile chametz—Jew wants chametz existence; therefore fruit juice—see his words:
(s.k. 3) Since, etc.—book of rabbanan—perhaps no saliva in them:

And even if you say, etc.—still Rama's words not settled—for he wrote since already nullified—implies unspecified nullified on eve; Magen Avraham intent for law: even if nullifies now before giving to animal—not effective as 448—even hefker animal forbidden chametz; though Magen Avraham 445:2 permits throw chametz to hefker pig though fear eats—here like gave before animal though not yet leavened:
(s.k. 4) Wall sweat as printed—and siman 453—meaning unlike those who read donkey sweat—for we hold 453 animal sweat does not leaven like human:
(s.k. 5) And some say—requires study—for contrary Rav's custom one view primary; here contrary 'some forbid' should be primary:

And Rosh did not dispute. Rokeach wrote wall sweat though not called liquid for impurity—for leavening called liquid like human saliva not making fit yet leavens.
